newsitem.title: POLAND: FORECAST-Polish 52-wk, 13-wk T-bill yield seen down.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Polish 52-wk, 13-wk T-bill yield seen down.

text.p: Banks expect the average yield on Poland's benchmark 52-week T-bill to fall to 18.57 percent at the end of 1997 against 21.93 percent at the last primary sale, a Reuters poll of the country's 26 largest banks showed.
Last month, banks saw the benchmark yield falling to 18.08 percent by year-end.
The end-1997 forecasts ranged from 17.00 to 20.60 percent.
Banks expected the 52-week average yield to ease to 17.67 percent in April 1998 with a range of forecasts of 16.00 to 19.50 percent.
They expected the yield to ease to 21.87 percent on average at the end of the month with a forecast range from 21.50 to 22.05 percent.
The average yield on the 13-week T-bill was also seen falling to 18.31 percent by year-end from 21.79 percent at the last primary auction, the poll showed.
Last month banks expected a yield fall to 17.74 percent.

The 13-week T-bill yield forecast is a mean average of banks' predictions ranging from 16.50 percent to 19.90 percent. The yield was seen falling to 17.39 percent in April 1998 with a forecast range between 14.75 and 19.00 percent.
Banks expected it to stay flat at 21.79 percent this month with a range from 21.40 to 22.10 percent.
